papers.title: Structured Problem Solving
papers.current_ceiling: The primitive-minimality promotion failed: AND and OR are both minimal singleton bases, so no unique indispensable primitive exists.
post_matrix_updates: The bounded formal OCME object remains useful, but no compute may be spent rescuing the old minimality claim.
load_bearing_adverse: G_DONOR fails under its own frozen operationalization.
Reordering primitives or rerunning the same minimality question is forbidden.
papers.strongest_remaining_gap: The successor must define outside-closure discovery operationally and show safe method-language expansion after donor-complete first refusal on objective-verifier domains.
papers.decisive_question: After a donor-complete method library is frozen, can an obstruction certificate identify tasks outside its closure and justify a new method that improves held-out verified reach without false expansion across at least three domains?
papers.maximum_claim_if_supported: Obstruction-certified method expansion safely enlarges a problem-solving language only when the current donor closure is demonstrably insufficient.
papers.hypothesis_or_theorem: A native verifier should confirm that proposed expansion targets lie outside donor closure, that the added method creates new held-out reach and that no expansion is authorized for inside-closure or unsolved cases.
papers.population_or_universe: Prospectively frozen tasks from at least three objective-verifier domains, including E12 and two of program repair, SAT/SMT, synthesis or retrieval with native correctness checks.
papers.unit_of_analysis: Task × frozen method library × proposed expansion.
design: Define method semantics and closure before selecting challenge tasks.
Require a native obstruction certificate before expansion.
Test the added method on protected held-out tasks and track false expansions.
Use distinct domains and independent verifier adapters.
baselines: Unrestricted search with matched total resources.
primary_endpoints: False expansion rate, with zero as a noncompensatory gate.
Resource-adjusted benefit and transfer across domains.
negative_controls: Task unsolved by both donor and proposed method.
Expansion that duplicates a donor under a renamed interface.
analysis_plan: Exact verifier outcomes and domain-level hierarchical synthesis.
No success from unrestricted extra resources.
papers.power_or_exhaustion_rule: Use all frozen eligible tasks per domain or a power plan based on design-only tasks; require protected positives and known no-expansion controls in every domain.
papers.success_gate: Zero false expansions, valid certificates and new verified held-out reach beyond the donor product in at least three domains under matched resources.
papers.refutation_gate: Any false expansion, donor-equivalent method or lack of protected new reach defeats the broad expansion claim.
papers.cannot_check_gate: CANNOT_CHECK if donor closure, verifier correctness, resource matching or method identity is ambiguous.
papers.authority_required: Native verifiers plus independent closure/certificate checker and donor-literature audit.

active_lane.collision_rule: New scientific identity only; the old primitive-minimality claim is closed and cannot be reordered or rerun.

immediate_safe_actions: Write an operational closure definition with extensional method equivalence.
Select three verifier-backed domains without reading candidate outcomes.
Build forged/inside-closure controls before any expansion run.
forbidden_actions: Do not call a renamed donor a new method.
Do not authorize expansion without an obstruction certificate.
papers.journal_bar: A top-tier automated-discovery paper needs donor-complete closure, native obstruction certificates, protected new reach, zero false expansion and cross-domain validation.
papers.sibling_boundary: Owns method-language expansion; state computation and online allocation belong to ORION-21/22.
